summary: Part 1 of 2 of "10.0 Quality guidelines (Seller & KAMs)" (00:00-03:57). Pierre walks through Revibe's Phones, tablets & watches quality guidelines deck: why the guidelines exist, the three grades (Excellent, Very good, Good), general and grade rules (hardware, screen, body, battery, camera dots, plug), parts rules, the functions deep dive, screen acceptance, and the banned-elements and claims-penalty policy. All 40 pack-1 frames were opened and each cited frame was matched to its caption and content. Many frame citations in the pack were off by one or two frames; they are corrected in audit.corrected. Narration-versus-screen conflicts are logged as unclear rather than stated as facts, including a new one: the Cameras row shows max 2 small dots for Very good and Good, while the grading table and narration say one for Very good.

'Total should never exceed 2 claims. If so, a trigger gets activated'

facts.statement: When the trigger is activated, claims are checked one by one. The screen says the Revibe team checks them; the narration says 'You, as a KM' (see unclear list).

evidence.quote: You, as a KM then check these claims one by one.
'Revibe team to check these claims one by one'

facts.statement: If a claim is confirmed, a 10% penalty applies to each claim received, based on the seller's price.

evidence.quote: If they're confirmed, a 10% penalty applies to each claim received based on the seller price.
'10% penalty applies on each claim received, based on the seller's price'

facts.statement: AI analyses customer claim forms in detail and flags the issues it spots. The narration says 'you' check the flagged claims, and if they are valid the seller gets a penalty for each one.

evidence.quote: Using AI, we'll analyze customer claim forms in detail.
When we spot one of these issues, we'll flag it to you.
You check the claims, and if they're valid, the seller gets a penalty for each one.
Caption 'AI flags them, you confirm'

facts.statement: Grading banned elements: a 'Excellent' device sold with visible scratches; battery health below the grade minimum (Good < 85%, Very good < 90%, Excellent < 95%); a 'New' device that must be non-active and sold in a box that has never been opened.

evidence.quote: '"Excellent" sold with visible scratches'; 'Battery health below the grade minimum: Good < 85%, Very good < 90%, Excellent < 95%'; '"New" must be non-active and sold in a box that has never been opened'

facts.statement: Wrong-item banned elements: wrong device shipped (wrong storage, colour or model); region variant mismatch such as Japan shutter sound or inability to use the device in the destination countries; missing in-box accessories (charger for laptops, cable for all devices).

evidence.quote: 'Wrong device shipped: wrong storage, colour or model'; 'Region variant mismatch such as Japan shutter sound...'; 'Missing in-box accessories (charger for laptops, cable for all devices)'

facts.statement: Parts banned elements: a non-original or fake S Pen on Samsung devices; a device displaying a spare-part replacement message (showing non-original parts) or a battery replacement alert.

evidence.quote: 'Non-original or fake S Pen on Samsung devices'; 'Device displaying a spare-part replacement message (showing non-original parts) or battery replacement alert'

facts.statement: Locks and IMEI banned elements: iCloud, Google account or MDM profile still active; blacklisted IMEI, or device reported lost or stolen; device not factory reset (previous user data still present); network or carrier-locked (SIM lock) device sold as unlocked.

evidence.quote: 'iCloud, Google account or MDM profile still active'; 'Blacklisted IMEI, or device reported lost or stolen'; 'Device not factory reset - previous user data still present'; 'Network / carrier-locked (SIM lock) device sold as unlocked'

terms.meaning: The three quality grades the guidelines are split into. Each device is rated against the rules for its grade.
Every device must be fully working in all grades, like a new one.
Minimum battery health per grade: 95% Excellent, 90% Very good, 85% Good. The screen adds 'match 3utool'.
The tool used to check battery health. The trainer calls it a free tool every seller can use. Spelled 3utool on screen.
A camera defect checked with the camera in portrait mode against white paper or a white wall. Limits: none (Excellent), 1 maximum (Very good), 2 maximum (Good), per the grading table.
A part type named in the table. Accepted for the display in Excellent, and required for the S Pen on Samsung. The video does not define it further.
A type of copy LCD that some suppliers use on phones. Accepted as the display in Excellent.
A copy part accepted for display, glass, cover, buttons and others. The device must not show a message about non-original parts.

terms.term: GW Good quality / GW & others Bad quality
terms.meaning: Column headings on the screen acceptance table for replacement screens. The abbreviation GW is not defined in the video.
A screen that is not original or DD, judged against the good-quality and bad-quality criteria.
An issue that should never be accepted in any grade or on any device, and should never lead to a claim.
A customer claim about a device. Claims are counted against the 2-claim limit and checked one by one.
What happens when a seller's total claims go above 2. The screen says the Revibe team checks the claims. Its full effect is not explained in the video.
The base for the 10% penalty per confirmed claim.
10% per claim received, when the claim is confirmed, based on the seller's price.
A message on the device showing non-original parts. It is a banned element.
An IMEI reported as blacklisted. It is a banned element.
A device locked to a network carrier. Selling it as unlocked is a banned element.
A device whose region variant does not suit the destination country, for example a Japan shutter sound or no ability to use the device in the destination countries.

asr_fixes.basis: Screen: Body row, Very good and Good columns (frame t00049) show 'May have a few light scratches that are not visible at first glance unless you look closely. Small'.
Screen: each battery cell reads 'minimum + match 3utool' (frames t00049 and t00061).
Screen: box text on the banned elements page reads 'based on the seller's price' (frame t00207).

unclear.issue: Good screen scratches. Narration says slight scratches are allowed 'as long as you can't see them when the screen is on'. The screen says 'Slight scratches may be visible, but they do not interfere when the appliance is switched on'. The rule differs (visibility vs interference). Confirm the official wording before quoting it to a seller.

Body test distance. Narration says body scratches for Very good and Good are 'invisible from 20 to 30 centimeters away'. The screen says 'not visible at first glance unless you look closely' and gives no distance. The 20 to 30 cm test is not confirmed on screen.

Camera dot limit for Excellent in the functions deep dive. The Cameras row (frame t00130) says 'All modes must work and max 1 small camera dot accepted' in the Excellent column. The Camera dot row (frame t00073) and the narration (01:18) say Excellent allows none. The Excellent limit is unresolved.

Camera dot limit for Very good. Narration says one small dot is accepted on very good (02:07, and 01:18 'very good one at most'). The Cameras row (frame t00130) puts Very good and Good in one merged cell: 'All modes must work and max 2 small camera dots accepted'. The Camera dot row says '1 small maximum' for Very good. The screen and narration conflict.

Who checks the claims. Narration says 'You, as a KM then check these claims one by one.' The screen says 'Revibe team to check these claims one by one' (frame t00207). The caption 'AI flags them, you confirm' (frames t00215, t00225) suggests the KAM confirms. The role is unresolved.
Term 'KM' in narration. The audience is Seller & KAM and the term is not on screen. It probably means KAM (key account manager), but this is not confirmed in the evidence.
Abbreviation 'GW' in the screen acceptance table headings (GW Good quality, GW & others Bad quality) is not defined in the video, and neither the narration nor the screen says what it stands for.

Label mismatch. Narration says the replacement screen 'looks light gray when off'. On screen the row that reads 'Light grey' is labelled 'Keyboard' (frame t00157). The label and what is described do not obviously match.

Scope of the 2-claim limit. The screen says 'Total should never exceed 2 claims' but does not say per seller, per period, or per order. Also the meaning of 'a trigger gets activated' beyond the Revibe team check is not explained.
Effective date. Narration says 'Under the new policy' and 'We're now introducing banned elements'. No effective date is given on screen or in the narration.
The meaning of 'match 3utool' in the battery row is not explained. The video does not show how the reading is matched.

Phone carrier wording on screen, 'Must be unlocked to a phone carrier' (frame t00119), is ambiguous. It is not clear whether it means carrier-unlocked or something else. Compare the banned element 'Network / carrier-locked (SIM lock) device sold as unlocked'.

outdated.signal: 'We're now introducing banned elements' and 'Under the new policy' (03:27): time-bound wording with no effective date on screen or in narration. The policy may have changed since the video was made.

privacy.what: A personal name appears at the top of the phone Settings screens in the pinkish-tint illustration. It is partly legible. It was not copied into this reference. Blur or crop before sharing with sellers.
The same personal name appears on the Settings screen in the same illustration.
